reason: The current MultVAE–SASRec ensemble achieves measured macro validation HR@10 of 0.6200, supporting retention of both trained members while testing only their fusion. Equal-weight mean ranks penalize every rank displacement linearly; reciprocal ranks may better preserve strong top-ranked evidence, although the HR@20–HR@10 gap does not establish fusion as the cause. Historical ensemble and 16-negative SASRec successes favor preserving those configurations, while failed loss-weighting experiments support isolating this inference change. Modify model_design for the shared fusion rule and training_evaluation for predictor consistency, diagnostics, and accurate reporting.

plan.model_design: Replace only the body of rank_fusion(vae_scores, sasrec_scores) with equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion: r_vae = descending_ranks(vae_scores).float() + 1.0, r_sasrec = descending_ranks(sasrec_scores).float() + 1.0, and return 1.0 / (10.0 + r_vae) + 1.0 / (10.0 + r_sasrec). Keep descending_ranks zero-based with stable candidate-order tie-breaking, converting to one-based ranks inside rank_fusion so other callers retain their existing semantics. This fixed nonlinear rule tests whether stronger top-ranked evidence improves HR@10 without introducing fitted weights, category-specific constants, raw-logit mixing, or additional parameters. Preserve variable names, function signatures, score_members, Ensemble.score, Ensemble.predict, both model architectures and forward passes, uniform-history reconstruction, and SASRec's existing positive-plus-16-negative cross-entropy training.
plan.training_evaluation: Preserve write_predict_script() and its predict(user_id, history, candidates, *, dataset_name=None) interface, ensuring the generated working/predict.py loads the modified training module and therefore uses the identical shared reciprocal-rank helper as local evaluate; update generated comments and validation JSON fusion metadata to identify equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion with constant 10 and one-based ranks. Replace the obsolete mean-rank fixture in check_history_transform with expected scores [1/11 + 1/13, 1/12 + 1/11, 1/14 + 1/12, 1/13 + 1/14] for its existing a and b tensors, retain the descending_ranks assertion, and preserve checkpoint-reload and generated-predictor agreement checks without consuming training RNG state. Explicitly keep unchanged both members' losses, negative sampling, optimizers, hyperparameters, initialization, checkpoint selection, validation cadence, patience, existing deadlines, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200; retain single-GPU execution and account for all execution within the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training and evaluation seeds 42, supplied splits, all four categories and dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and the pinned evaluation protocol of 200 validation users per category with 99 unique negatives; leave the host evaluator and held-out prediction ownership unchanged and access no hidden test files. Report measured category scores and macro validation HR@10 against 0.6200, including any decline, retain the final measured-score print, and treat the proposed 0.005–0.015 gain solely as an unverified hypothesis.
